newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products lose ground on crude, muted trade.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products lose ground on crude, muted trade.

text.p: Med oil products were weakened on Friday by easier crude futures in a thin market.
Gasoline fell under pressure from weaker NWE spot and NYMEX futures markets as buyers stayed scarce.

Traders blamed the lack of demand across Europe, the scarcity of vessels to take product to the U.S. and gasoline's recent strength in relation to naphtha, that has caused both refiners and blenders to maximise output.
Physical naphtha trade remained dull with demand for most grades thin. Traders said the spot market should still have an overhang but scarce buyers saw nothing offered to support this.
Cargoes were notionally around $217.50 a tonne cif Med.

Gas oil shed $4.25 a tonne with softer futures. Fresh demand emerged for 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil, with inquiries from five major oil companies lifting premiums notionally to around cif high quotes +$1 basis Genoa from around flat.
A 20-25,000 tonne Russian for Jan 10-20 was bid at high cif quotes +$1.50, attracting an offer at +$2. Another Russian was sought on an exchange for physical basis at Feb IPE +$3.
But activity was modest with many players still away on leave. "The real market will show its true colours next week," a cargo trader said.

Fuel oil activity perked up on Friday with a high sulphur cargo sold ex-Italy and material heard traded from Greece. Traders said demand for bunker spec material was also likely to have been met. A Jan paper deal was done at $109 fob Med.
The main Med buyer for low sulphur cracked fuel remained out of the market and prices were seen to have eased in line with easier northern numbers.
